# The AI Revolution: Who Wins, Who Loses & the SaaSpocalypse | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 70

First listed: 2026-07-27 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The AI Revolution: Who Wins, Who Loses & the SaaSpocalypse | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 70](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SWEzkOMe4tY) - 2026-07-27
- [Substack: The AI Revolution: Who Wins, Who Loses & the SaaSpocalypse](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-ai-revolution-who-wins-who-loses) - 2026-07-27

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Dan Ives and Gil Luria argue for an extended AI buildout while differentiating infrastructure, model and application economics. Eisman challenges capital intensity, weak model moats and Chinese price competition. The episode contains genuine Ives/Luria Oracle revisions, conditional Apple and cybersecurity theses, and overbroad guest claims about software debt and productivity necessarily creating jobs. Eisman retains model-moat doubts in his closing recap.

Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.

- [Oracle Q4 and FY2026 results](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Record-Q4-and-FY-2026-Results-Driven-by-Cloud-Infrastructure--Cloud-Applications/default.aspx) (2026-06-10): RPO $638 billion, adjusted EPS $2.11 up 24%, fiscal-year OCF $32b and FCF negative $23.7b imply $55.7b capex. FY27 financing plan approximately $40b; prepaid/customer-supplied hardware reduces funding needs.

### 046. Doubling employee productivity necessarily doubles company revenue and therefore causes hiring rather than job cuts.

**Wrong** | Gil Luria | analytical principle | major

The claimed necessity does not follow from microeconomics; demand response and prices matter.

Conditional reasoning: Required employment falls from Q/a to Q/(2a) while revenue remains price times Q. This counterexample disproves the claimed necessary doubling of revenue and hiring. Expanded demand can instead increase employment, but requires additional assumptions.

## Framework and tools

- Disaggregate the AI value chain before applying one bullish or bearish narrative.
- Question crowding and update when counterparty funding changes.
- Translate backlog into funded, delivered, margin-generating revenue.
- Separate low P/E from true undervaluation across cyclical earnings bases.
- Distinguish technology adoption from shareholder returns.
- Preserve exploratory challenges and guest opinions separately from adopted host forecasts.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- AI lab annualized revenue versus cumulative capex
- Oracle backlog, customer funding and reverse valuation
- Micron/NVIDIA versus Intel/AMD forward P/E comparison
- Model price and capability comparison
- Cybersecurity budget-doubling scenario
